notes: National Rail (Darwin/OpenLDBWS) is structurally catalogued here but blocked at the account level — DARWIN_LDB_TOKEN not set. Same blocker as every other UK region in this wave.

Metrolink: TfGM developer portal (opendata.tfgm.com) is deprecated and no longer issues new API keys; no confirmed GTFS-RT feed exists anywhere. Genuinely unconfirmed feed status (same kind as South Yorkshire's Supertram/SYFTL gap), not the standard National Rail account block. fetchMetrolinkStopBoard() in lib/providers/greater-manchester.js throws MetrolinkFeedUnconfirmedError rather than fabricating a schedule. See docs/greater-manchester-d1/hazard-pack.md and jim-handoff.md skip risk section.

TWO AGENCIES, TWO HUB+SECONDARY-HUB PAIRS, cross-linked at one shared-building station (Manchester Victoria) — a deliberate departure from the oracle report's own single-sentence headline recommendation (C2/C3 point 4, 'hub lock: Victoria'), built instead from the report's own supporting facts (line 22: Piccadilly 14 platforms/all six TOCs vs Victoria 6 platforms/two TOCs). See docs/greater-manchester-d1/jim-handoff.md and direction-model-memo.md for the full reasoning — do not 'simplify' this back to a single Victoria hub lock without re-reading it.
National Rail hub lock: Manchester Piccadilly (MAN). National Rail secondary hub: Manchester Victoria (MCV). Metrolink hub lock: St Peter's Square. Metrolink secondary hub: Manchester Victoria.

Manchester Victoria is built ONCE as a shared-building station — one printed name, two catalog entries (mode train, mode metro), doNotGroup: true between them. Same shape as Sheffield Station (South Yorkshire) and Nottingham Station (East Midlands): escalator/lift connect, ~2-5 min walk within one shared concourse, not a cross-platform interchange.

Manchester Piccadilly (National Rail, MAN) and Piccadilly Gardens (Metrolink) are TWO SEPARATE stationGroups, doNotGroup: true between them — a walk-link pair (~100m, 5-10 min via moving walkways, undercroft vs street-level), NOT a shared building the way Victoria is. Closer in shape to West Yorkshire's Bradford Forster Square/Bradford Interchange pair. Never merge these two under one printed name.

No Metrolink stop at Stockport — the earlier 'two Stockports' hazard was an error (7 Sep 2026). Manchester Metrolink has never served Stockport; a Stockport extension has only been proposed. The catalog's former 'Stockport (tram stop)' entry did not exist and has been removed. See docs/jim-brief-net-toton-lane-and-stockport-tram.md.

Walsden (WDN CRS): through-running-only boundary station toward West Yorkshire on the Calder Valley Line, single operator (Northern), same platform, not a merge. CRS CODE MISMATCH, NOT RESOLVED: this region's own oracle report gives WDN; West Yorkshire's already-merged pack (lib/cities/west-yorkshire/stations.json) gives WAD for the same physical station. Neither is authoritative — this catalog uses WDN because that is what THIS region's own oracle report gives, per the dispatch instruction not to silently pick one. Flagged for Tim/Nico to resolve against a live Darwin response or National Rail's published CRS list before either code is trusted. Do NOT edit West Yorkshire's stations.json to 'fix' this.

Metrolink line arrays (see marketing-directions.js) are TERMINI-ONLY per the oracle report's C2/C3 point 10 summary — NOT a full ordered 99-stop list. Only the hub, secondary hub, and named termini/via-points from that summary are catalogued below; the remaining ~85 of 99 Metrolink stops are a real, uncatalogued gap. Do not treat this list as complete.

Green and Purple Metrolink lines share the same terminus pair (Altrincham-Bury) with opposite line names/colours — the report does not explain the routing difference. Not resolved here; do not guess which physical routing distinguishes them.

The Eccles line's 'Manchester' terminus (as printed in the oracle report) is NOT catalogued as a station here — genuinely ambiguous which physical Manchester stop this refers to, not given by the report. Do not guess a resolution; the Eccles Line + Manchester chip is left as an unresolved marketing string only, generated (if at all) from the Eccles terminus, never as a resolvable catalog entry.

'Piccadilly' as printed in the oracle report's Metrolink line-termini table (Yellow, Airport lines) refers to the Piccadilly Gardens Metrolink stop, NOT Manchester Piccadilly National Rail station — aliased accordingly below. Never conflate the two; see doNotUse list in docs/greater-manchester-d1/published-network.json.

Metrolink lat/lng superseded 7 Sep 2026 (uk-catalog-geocode) — NaPTAN carries confirmed stop-level coordinates (StopType TMU, ATCO prefix 1800ZZMA / "(Manchester Metrolink)" suffix) independent of the GTFS-RT feed gap noted elsewhere, which is about real-time data, not the stop registry. 14/14 stops matched — the earlier 'Stockport (tram stop)' entry that failed to geocode was removed 7 Sep 2026 as a non-existent stop, not left as an unresolved gap.

Coordinates: NaPTAN RailReferences (CRS->coords) pulled 2026-09-07; 4/4 rail stations geocoded | NaPTAN StopType TMU (ATCO prefix 1800ZZMA / "(Manchester Metrolink)" suffix) pulled 2026-09-07; 14/14 tram/metro stops geocoded; no exceptions

7 Sep 2026 (docs/jim-brief-no-live-feed-stops-out-of-picker.md): all 14 Metrolink (mode metro) stops flagged liveFeed: false — MetrolinkFeedUnconfirmedError means no board can ever be produced, so these stops stay in the catalog (coordinates kept for coverage notes and a future re-enable) but are no longer offered in the station picker or Near me. National Rail (mode train) stops are unaffected.
